rulings.Case Title: MEGAN BROGGER VS. NOCTURNAL CODE, UNKNOWN ENTITY ET AL
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Tuesday, August 11, 2026, Line 3, CROSS DEFENDANT LISA ROSE's MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT. Cross-defendant Lisa Rose's motion for summary judgment is granted. Based on the deemed admissions of cross-complainant Tatiana Shiff, especially the deemed admissions that Shiff cannot identify any negligent act by Rose and cannot identify any act or omission by Rose that caused the injury claimed by plaintiff Megan Brogger or the movable partition wall to fall, Rose satisfied her summary judgment burden of showing that Shiff cannot prove any of her five claims against Rose. The burden then shifted to Shiff to present admissible evidence that there is a triable issue as to any of her claims. Shiff did not present any such evidence. The court exercised its discretion to consider Shiff's late-filed opposition papers. Shiff's efforts to dispute facts that she is deemed to admit are not permitted and do not create a triable issue. To the extent that they do not contradict facts that Shiff is deemed to admit, none of the facts presented by Shiff show that Rose committed any negligent act or omission or that Rose was in any way at fault for the injuries claimed by Brogger and thus Rose is entitled to summary judgment on all five of Shiff's claims. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 302 Zoom ID 160 409 7690; Passcode 516287.) rulings.Case Title: ABIMBOLA AJAYI VS. CITY & COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO, ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Amended Consolidated Notice Of Motion And Motion For Protective Ordder To Limit Defendants' Expert Testimony (Evid. Code 720); And For Monetary And Evidentiary Sanctions For Bad Faith Litigation Tacts Of Discovery Misuse Of The Discovery Process (C.C.P. 2023.010, 2012.030)
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Tuesday, August 11, 2026, Line 4, PLAINTIFF ABIMBOLA AJAYI's Amended Consolidated Motion For Protective Order To Limit Defendants' Expert Testimony (Evid. Code 720); And For Monetary And Evidentiary Sanctions For Bad Faith Litigation Tacts Of Discovery Misuse Of The Discovery Process (C.C.P. 2023.010, 2012.030). Plaintiff Abimbola Ajayi's motion for protective order to limit defendants' expert testimony is denied as premature. With the trial continued to May 17, 2027 and all pre-trial deadlines triggered off of the new trial date, expert disclosures, including any revised disclosure concerning Dr. Frank Farrell, and expert depositions will not occur for many months. The concern that prompted this motion -- that an expert should not be designated or encouraged to testify about matters beyond her expertise -- is valid. However, the determination of whether a particular expert proposes to testify beyond her expertise almost always depends on the matters for which the expert is designated and the opinions expressed at a deposition. The April 23 email was a privileged communication that was inadvertently sent to plaintiff and is not covered by the narrow crime-fraud exception and henceforth must not be referred to by plaintiff in any filings or communications. This motion was motivated by a good faith concern that defendants are or might be intending to elicit opinions from their experts beyond the experts' expertise and thus, while unsuccessful, the motion does not lack substantial justification, so defendants' requests for monetary sanctions are denied.
